description: This week, the House passed major education reform bills. The Georgia Early Literacy Act of 2026 was passed by the House. This marks the largest education initiative since the passage of the HOPE Scholarship. This bill will allocate funding through the Quality Basic Education formula to provide literacy coaches for every public school, ensuring that every student is reading at grade level by grade 3. It also establishes a Georgia Literacy Task Force to ensure oversight. It further provides professional learning grounded in the science of reading for teachers and literacy coaches to ensure consistency in statewide literacy teaching. The Math Matters Act, HB 1030, requires all students who test at the end of 7th grade as “Distinguished” learners to be automatically placed in an Enhanced Math class. It requires 60 minutes of math instruction time for students in grades 4 and 5. It will allow students and their parents to decide whether to opt out of advanced math classes, ensuring this choice isn’t determined solely by the teacher. The Distraction-Free Education Act, HB 1009, builds on last year’s cell phone ban in schools by extending it to high schools. Students with an IEP or medical plan will be able to access devices as necessary. School Safety, HB 1023, will require local school boards to implement one or more weapon detection systems at all main points of entry for permanent school buildings in Georgia’s public schools to prevent individuals from unlawfully bringing weapons onto school campuses. Expanding Access to After-School Programs, HB 1123, will expand access to after-school programs to help working families. Public schools that offer after-care programs to students in kindergarten, primary, or upper elementary grades and that also operate pre-K programs will be required to make those programs available to pre-K students on the same basis. Financial Transparency, HB 1164, will require the State Board of Education establish an audit committee and define its duties. It updates the financial audit rules for school districts and charter schools. The Department of Audits and Accounts will develop a tiered monitoring system to assess the financial health of these entities. If a school is flagged as financially distressed, specific intervention strategies will be implemented.
title: Week 7 recap, Insurance and Education Reform.-Rep. Carmen Rice
